title: Mar Zutra son of Rav Nachman
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman places him among the leading sages of the generation in Rava’s time, and both received from Rav Nachman, as in [Beitzah 34b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.34b.3-5), where Rava asked Rav Nachman and Mar Zutra said of this, “We too have learned it.”

In [Sotah 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.10a.14) he asked Rav Nachman, “What is podagra like?” In [Gittin 50a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.50a.5-6) he spoke in Rav Nachman’s name, and Abaye said, “Know.” In [Bava Batra 151b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.151b.4): “The Rabbis said it before Rava in the name of Mar Zutra son of Rav Nachman, who said it in Rav Nachman’s name”; and so it is in [Avodah Zarah 37b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.37b.8). In [Bava Batra 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.7a.4) Hyman considers “before Rabbah” erroneous and proposes “Rava.”

In [Chullin 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.94b.13) he was going from Sikhra to Bei Mechoza, and Rava and Rav Safra were coming to Sikhra; they met each other. He (Mar Zutra) thought they were coming to meet him, and said to them: “Why did the Rabbis trouble so much?” Rav Safra said to him: “We did not know that the Master was coming; had we known, we would have troubled more.” His halakhot we find in [Berakhot 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.43b.15), [Shabbat 88b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.88b.4) and [96a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.96a.1), [Bava Metzia 4b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.4b.11) and [88b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.88b.6); and his well-known ruling in [Gittin 49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.49b.9-11), that he holds a woman’s ketubah is collected from middle-grade land when she collects directly from her husband,[^3] on which Abaye and Rava said, “Come and hear.” Hyman cites Horayot 13a; in the consulted passage [Horayot 13a:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.13a.16) Mar Zutra says “Come and hear.” Hyman connects this to Rami bar Chama’s question, and some say he himself resolved it, saying, “Did Rava not report a teaching in Rav Nachman’s name on this?” (see Rashi there).[^4] Hyman cites Berakhot 54b for Mar Zutra’s reply to Rav Huna (Hon) son of Rav Nachman in defense of Rava. Compare [Bekhorot 54b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.54b.7). [Sanhedrin 5a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.5a.3) relates that he judged a case and erred; he came before Rav Yosef, who said to him: “If they accepted you over them, you need not pay.” Learn from this that when one does not take authorization, his judgment is a valid judgment. Of his personal deeds we find that he was wealthy and scrupulous in his deeds, as in [Moed Katan 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.12a.4): they built him a mansion by contract outside the boundary (on Shabbat); Rav Safra and Rav Huna bar Chinena visited and did not go in to him; some say he too did not go into it.

notes.text: The positive conclusion is retained: supplied דיניה דינא and saved Davidson Sanhedrin5a paragraph2 both conclude a judgment without authorization IS valid. The draft’s not a judgment is withdrawn. Restore the supplied Hon parenthetical. ר״ג in Gittin is expanded to Nachman contextually, disclosed; the case remains abridged. Hyman’s Rabbah-to-Rava proposal remains attributed.

The consulted Sanhedrin 5a explicitly concludes that judgment without authorization is valid, while distinguishing liability when the parties did not accept the judge. The withdrawn negative conclusion is not restored. Hon, the Nachman siglum and Hyman’s Rabbah/Rava proposal remain disclosed. His leading-generation and personal-life conclusions are not independently established by this one case.

[Gittin 49b:9–11](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.49b.9-11) distinguishes collection directly from the husband from collection from his heirs, where Mar Zutra gives the lower grade. The phrase “before Rabbah” appears in [Bava Batra 7a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.7a.4); Hyman proposes Rava. [Seder HaDorot 1097](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1097&lang=en) lists several of Mar Zutra son of Rav Nachman’s named transmissions. Heilprin points to [Bekhorot 54b:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.54b.7). There Rav Huna objects and Mar Zutra defends Rava’s reading. The Hebrew directs Mar Zutra’s reply to Rava, whereas the accompanying English directs it to Rav Huna, as Hyman does.

In the linked Horayot passage, Mar Zutra son of Rav Nachman says “Come and hear” and cites a baraita about burial when a deputy High Priest and a priest anointed for war encounter a body. The linked paragraph does not name Rami bar Chama or include Hyman’s alternative formulation.
